calendar.impact: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 13 is the first inventory test of the surplus pricing, with the industry estimate at a 5.28 million barrel crude build against a survey consensus of 1.0 million. The last dated outage in the window is scheduled to resume operations the same day.
calendar.title: EIA report for week ending Nov 13, and Irving Osprey resumption date

calendar.impact: The December WTI contract expires Friday, which puts the front differential's first trade, whenever it comes, inside the expiry week for a second straight month.
calendar.title: December WTI expiry

calendar.impact: Shareholders vote on the plan of arrangement under which Cenovus acquires Athabasca, with closing expected in December.
calendar.title: Athabasca special meeting on the Cenovus arrangement

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the IEA printing a fourth-quarter surplus and Goldman pencilling a 2.0 million barrel a day surplus for 2027.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: The surplus is moving from forecast to stock test: an industry build of 5.28 million barrels against a 1.0 million consensus is what today's report grades, while the basin balance keeps tanking toward December storage of 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity and the December apportionment notice stays unpublished.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled $93.14, up $0.70, and WTI Dec26 settled $86.01, up $0.29, on Tuesday (Reuters, Nov 17), and Asia gave the recovery back to Brent $92.53 and WTI $84.77 at 0550 GMT on Wednesday (Reuters, Nov 18). WTI fell roughly twice as hard as Brent and the Brent to WTI spread widened from $7.13 at the settle toward a more than two-week high. The industry estimate for the week ending Nov 13 printed crude up 5.28 million barrels and gasoline up 5.12 million against a survey consensus of 1.0 and 1.4 million. Brent's prompt spread is still backwardated at about $2.80, against more than $3 a month ago.
changes.conditional: An official build near the industry estimate extends the surplus pricing into the front spreads; a draw against both the industry estimate and the survey reopens the question of whether Monday's fall was liquidation rather than information, on a positioning book that was already washed out.
changes.delta: Asia unwound Tuesday's recovery with WTI falling about twice as hard as Brent, the spread widening to a more than two-week high, and the industry inventory estimate printing well above consensus ahead of today's report
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 17 and 18, 2026; API via Reuters market sources, Nov 17, 2026; Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones survey, Nov 17, 2026
changes.title: The recovery faded on the inventory build, and the spread, not flat price, took the strain
changes.vintage: Reuters settles, Nov 17, 2026, and overnight tape at 0550 GMT, Nov 18, 2026

changes.balance: The confirmed tempo now carries a human cost and a direct US and Iran exchange of fire, but the measured flow gauge has not moved in a week; the strait's risk pricing stays live without a confirmed new barrel removed, and the flow print, not the incident count, is still what converts tempo into supply.
changes.body: UKMTO Warning 208-26 was updated on Nov 17: a second strike and another fire were reported on the vessel attacked north of Khasab on Nov 16, with the crew unaccounted for. Indian authorities identified the vessel as the Panama-flagged LPG carrier Tara Gas, with subsequent Indian reporting of one seafarer missing and two injured. The IRGC said it targeted a US radar system in Bahrain on Nov 17, US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island, and Bahrain intercepted further Iranian aerial attacks early on Nov 18. Iranian claims of six tankers struck since Sunday remain unconfirmed. Kpler's latest measured clearance, to Nov 11, is 8,264 kb/d, 48 percent of pre-war.
changes.conditional: A fresh measured clearance print materially below 8,264 kb/d, or a confirmed halt to loadings, converts the tempo into a supply event; continued incidents at the current measured clearance keep the surplus in charge of the front month.
changes.delta: The Khasab vessel was reported struck a second time with one seafarer missing, and the US and Iran exchanged fire directly on Nov 17, while the latest measured clearance stays a week old
changes.source: UKMTO Warning 208-26 Update 001, Nov 17, 2026; Reuters, Nov 17 to 18, 2026; Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026
changes.title: A second strike on the Khasab vessel and a direct US and Iran exchange, on a week-old flow gauge

changes.balance: December WCS remains a mark into an apportionment notice that has not published a day after the close that sets it; the traded deferred tightening says the winter strip is wide but not widening, and the notice is the next physical print on the front.
changes.body: December WCS settled -$28.22 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 17) on zero lots, a ninth straight session without a December trade, with December outright at $57.79 on Tuesday's WTI settle. The traded strip tightened for a second day: Jan27 -$24.75, up $1.00 on 500 lots, Feb27 -$23.25 on 45 lots and Mar27 -$22.30, and January's ARV to TMW spread printed +$8.00. November apportionment stands at Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert. December nominations closed Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST and no December notice had been published as of this morning's check, so the registered December call of Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent remains ungraded.
changes.conditional: A December notice at or above the registered call, or a first December trade materially wider than -$28.22, reopens the widening path; a lighter notice with the deferred tightening held extends the snap-back in the traded strip.
changes.delta: December WCS marked -$28.22 on zero lots for a ninth straight session while the traded deferred strip tightened a dollar on volume, and the December notice stayed unpublished after the nominations close
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 17, 2026; Enbridge notice, Oct 20, 2026
changes.title: The front month is still a mark, the traded strip tightened again, and the notice is late

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. December nominations closed Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST and the Enbridge notice that grades the call had not been published as of the Nov 18 morning check. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December front month that has not traded in nine sessions, and deferred strip tightening on volume for two straight days.
flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, and the notice is unpublished a day after the close
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice, or a material change in the physical backdrop before it publishes

flags.body: Two tanker incidents are confirmed in the current cycle: the outbound vessel in Warning 207-26 on Nov 16, crew accounted for, and the vessel in Warning 208-26 north of Khasab, reported struck a second time on Nov 17 with one seafarer missing and two injured on Indian reporting. The US and Iran exchanged fire directly on Nov 17 and Bahrain intercepted further attacks early Nov 18. Iranian claims of six tankers struck since Sunday carry no named vessel and no confirmation. Kpler's latest measured clearance is 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11, 48 percent of pre-war, and is now a week old. A confirmed flow interruption reprices the strait; continued incidents at the current measured clearance keep the surplus in charge.
flags.title: Confirmed tempo is rising and the flow gauge is a week old: clearance 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11
flags.trigger: A fresh measured clearance print materially below 8,264 kb/d, or confirmation of a loadings halt from a tracker, owner or UKMTO product

flags.body: The industry estimate for the week ending Nov 13 printed crude up 5.28 million barrels and gasoline up 5.12 million, against a Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones survey consensus of crude up 1.0 million and gasoline up 1.4 million. The official report lands Nov 18 at 10:30 a.m. ET. The industry estimate has had the direction right four straight weeks while the official report confirmed only a fraction of its magnitude in each of the last two. A confirmed build near the industry estimate turns the surplus from a forecast into a stock level; a draw against both estimates reopens the pricing.
flags.title: Inventory test today: industry build of 5.28 million against a 1.0 million consensus
flags.trigger: The EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending Nov 13, released Nov 18 at 10:30 a.m. ET
